note: Models artifact A03 (Phiếu thu thập số liệu / CRF) from Phase_3.pdf's artifact catalog — the one genuinely Word-renderable, human-facing deliverable of the phase's own 'reader layer' that plausibly starts from a fill-in-the-blanks template. The other five .docx artifacts that spec names (A05 consent form, A08 readable analysis plan, B03 standardization minutes, B04 research diary, D03 results tables) are either machine-rendered from a JSON source of truth (codebook.json/analysis_plan.json/results.json) rather than user-typed content, or need their own separate format entries — flagged for a human decision, not silently built here. The actual variable list (age, sex, VAS, BMI, etc. in the phase's own codebook.json example) is inherently study-specific — different studies collect different variables — so only the universal CRF header/footer convention is locked; the variable list itself is entirely open. The header-field block (study code/subject code/collection date) is a real 2-column table, matching the confirmed-real table layout of idea-proposal.default's own header fields (same 'phiếu' form convention family) — Phase_3.pdf itself is a spec document, not a filled real CRF, so this is a disclosed convention, not an independently-verified fact from this specific phase's own source. The collector-signature line has a small blank space added below it for the actual signature — an enhancement, not extracted content. Every fillIn node carries a stable attrs.slotId — see format-registry/answers-merge.ts, which uses it to merge a separate, private per-project document-answers.json into this shared skeleton at export time.

attrs.note: Study-assigned subject code, e.g. NC001 — never a name or patient record number, per Phase_3.pdf section 2.4.
Open — the actual variable list is entirely defined by this study's own codebook.json (variable name, label, type, valid values); it cannot be fixed here without assuming a specific study.
